question:
**Case Study 7 (Social Networks – Follower Analysis):**

A microblogging site analyzes following patterns among a group $B = \{P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4\}$. Define the relation $F$ on $B$ as: $(P_i, P_j) \in F$ if and only if $P_i$ follows $P_j$ and $P_j$ follows $P_i$.

(a) Prove whether $F$ is an equivalence relation.

(b) Suppose there are only two mutual-follower pairs: $(P_1, P_2)$, $(P_2, P_1)$, and $(P_3, P_4)$, $(P_4, P_3)$. Write all equivalence classes.

(c) How many total possible relations can be defined on set $B$?
explanation:
(a)

*Reflexivity*: $(P_i, P_i) \in F$ only if $P_i$ follows themselves, which may not always be true. So, unless self-following is allowed, not reflexive.

*Symmetry*: If $(P_i, P_j) \in F$, $P_i$ follows $P_j$ and $P_j$ follows $P_i$, so $(P_j, P_i) \in F$. So, symmetric.

*Transitivity*: If $(P_1, P_2), (P_2, P_3) \in F$, does $(P_1, P_3) \in F$? Not necessarily, only if all follow each other.

So, generally, $F$ is only symmetric.

(b)

Assuming no self-following.

Given pairs: $(P_1, P_2)$, $(P_2, P_1)$; $(P_3, P_4)$, $(P_4, P_3)$.

Equivalence classes:

$[P_1] = [P_2] = \{P_1, P_2\}$

$[P_3] = [P_4] = \{P_3, P_4\}$

(c) **Total possible relations on set $B$: **

$\text{Number of elements in } B = 4$

$\text{Total ordered pairs in } B \times B = 4 \times 4 = 16$

$\text{Each ordered pair can either be included or not included in the relation}$

$\text{Total possible relations} = 2^{16} = 65536$

options.A:
(a) $F$ is always an equivalence relation.
(b) The only equivalence class is $B$.
(c) Total possible relations on $B$ are $4^2=16$.
options.B:
(a) In general, $F$ is symmetric but not necessarily reflexive or transitive, so it is not necessarily an equivalence relation.
(b) With the given mutual-follower pairs, the groups are $\{P_1,P_2\}$ and $\{P_3,P_4\}$, assuming self-pairs are included for equivalence-class interpretation.
(c) Since $|B\times B|=16$, total possible relations on $B$ are $2^{16}=65536$.
options.C:
(a) $F$ is reflexive but not symmetric.
(b) The classes are $\{P_1\},\{P_2\},\{P_3\},\{P_4\}$.
(c) Total possible relations are $2^4=16$.
options.D:
(a) $F$ is transitive only.
(b) No grouping is possible even if self-pairs are included.
(c) Total possible relations are $4!=24$.
